question: Which native Steam action and receiver can an opt-in VR psychoscope gesture use while retaining game restrictions?
claim: toggle_scope is registered from action table +0x968 to RVA 0x1590CC0. Its receiver is ArkPlayerInput embedded at live ArkPlayer+0x8E0, with owner backlink +0x70. The handler checks native L3, movement and cinematic conditions and calls the unlock-aware scope toggle.
method: Read-only Ghidra MCP decompilation, instruction listing, xrefs and raw bytes on explicitly selected /Prey/PreyDll.dll (bridge version not reported). Python 3.12 tools/re/verify_psychoscope.py independently reads the Steam PE, checks its SHA-256, full handler, producer/registration/receiver anchors and rel32 callees. An altered-byte negative control is refused.

identity.reason: Ghidra program identity and independent on-disk SHA-256 agree on Steam 7d6e322f...; x64 PE32+, image base 0x180000000.

instrument.reason: Ghidra action registration and complete handler disassembly agree with independently read PE bytes and decoded relative call targets.

control.reason: The full 208-byte shipping handler comparison passes; a modified byte is rejected. String producer and registration use the same +0x968 field.

scene.reason: Static analysis only; no scene or running game involved.

restore.reason: The binary and game were not mutated.

baseline.reason: No in-game baseline was run; the user restricted this batch to code/static work. Offline regressions are recorded separately and are not native acceptance.

limits: Steam build only. EGS symbols were search leads, not transferred addresses. No runtime or headset acceptance, progression-state test, or gesture ergonomics claim. Returning from the handler is only dispatch evidence. Graph refresh/intake await canonical checkout availability.

artifacts.role: Ghidra native producer, registration, receiver and consumer extracts
Independent Steam PE verification and negative control
Compiled native handler and receiver contract
